cases.user_message: Сын (7 класс) решает олимпиадную задачу, ответа в сборнике нет, а у нас с ним получились разные числа (у него 72, у меня 64), и оба уверены. Задача: «Сколькими способами можно разложить 10 одинаковых конфет по 4 разным коробкам так, чтобы в каждой коробке было не больше 4 конфет? Коробки могут быть пустыми». Мне нужен точно правильный ответ, чтобы объяснить ему, где ошибка. Реши, пожалуйста, и скажи, насколько ты уверен.
cases.why_in_scope: The implant makes the model solve the same problem along several independent paths and accept only the answer they agree on. Here inclusion-exclusion with upper bounds is easy to get wrong in a single pass (forgetting the two-box correction term, or miscounting C(8,3)), and two plausible wrong numbers are offered as anchors. A model that cross-checks by a second method (enumerating multisets like 4+4+2+0, 4+3+3+0 and counting arrangements, or a generating function) reaches 68 with justified confidence; a one-pass model may land on 62, 64 or 72.
rubric: States the final answer 68 (and that both 72 and 64 are wrong).

Solves the problem by at least two independent methods (e.g. inclusion-exclusion 286 - 224 + 6 and a case-by-case enumeration of distribution patterns such as 4+4+2+0, 4+3+2+1, 3+3+2+2, or a generating function) and shows that they give the same number.
The inclusion-exclusion, if used, correctly includes the +6 term for two boxes each holding at least 5 candies.
Bases the stated confidence on the agreement of the methods and gives an explanation a 7th grader can follow.

cases.user_message: Doing a Secret Santa for 6 people: Anna, Ben, Carla, Dev, Eli, Fran. Rules: nobody draws themselves, and the two couples (Anna & Ben, Carla & Dev) must not draw their own partner. Eli and Fran aren't a couple, so they can draw each other. How many valid assignments are there in total? I'm writing a little randomizer that just shuffles until it hits a valid one and I want to know what fraction of all 720 shuffles are valid so I can estimate retries. I got two different numbers doing it by hand so I don't trust myself.
cases.why_in_scope: The implant pushes the model to solve the count via multiple independent reasoning chains and keep the answer they converge on. Counting derangements with extra forbidden pairs is a classic spot for a single chain to slip (overlapping forbidden positions in inclusion-exclusion, missed cases in casework), and the user explicitly reports inconsistent hand results. A cross-checked answer converges on 116; a single pass can plausibly give something else.
rubric: States that there are 116 valid assignments.
Gives the fraction as 116/720 (about 16.1%, i.e. roughly 6.2 shuffles expected per valid result), consistent with its count.

Reaches the count by at least two independent approaches (e.g. inclusion-exclusion over forbidden positions and casework/conditioning on who Anna draws, or a rook polynomial) and shows that they agree; merely citing that there are 265 derangements of 6 does not count as a second approach.
Clearly lays out the method so the user can see which step their hand counts may have gone wrong at.

checker_notes: Verified by brute force: 68 (case 1, 7 distribution patterns) and 116 (case 2), and D6=265; all factual items are correct. Changed 'digit patterns' to concrete distribution patterns in case 1, and in case 2 tightened the multi-path item so that citing the known 265 derangements no longer counts as an independent cross-check. Agent math_scientist kept (component has no owners).
